lines.text: You pull’d me by the cloak; would you speak with me?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ay, Casca, tell us what hath chanc’d today,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That Caesar looks so sad.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Why, you were with him, were you not?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I should not then ask Casca what had chanc’d.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Why, there was a crown offer’d him; and being offer’d him, he put it by

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: with the back of his hand, thus; and then the people fell a-shouting.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What was the second noise for?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Why, for that too.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: They shouted thrice: what was the last cry for?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Why, for that too.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Was the crown offer’d him thrice?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Ay, marry, was’t, and he put it by thrice, every time gentler than

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: other; and at every putting-by mine honest neighbours shouted.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Who offer’d him the crown?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Why, Antony.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Tell us the manner of it, gentle Casca.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: I can as well be hang’d, as tell the manner of it: it was mere foolery;

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: I did not mark it. I saw Mark Antony offer him a crown; yet ’twas not a

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: crown neither, ’twas one of these coronets; and, as I told you, he put

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: it by once: but, for all that, to my thinking, he would fain have had

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: it. Then he offered it to him again: then he put it by again: but, to

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: my thinking, he was very loath to lay his fingers off it. And then he

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: offered it the third time; he put it the third time by; and still, as

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: he refus’d it, the rabblement hooted, and clapp’d their chopt hands,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: and threw up their sweaty night-caps, and uttered such a deal of

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: stinking breath because Caesar refus’d the crown, that it had, almost,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: choked Caesar, for he swooned, and fell down at it. And for mine own

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: part, I durst not laugh, for fear of opening my lips and receiving the

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: bad air.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But, soft! I pray you. What, did Caesar swoon?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: He fell down in the market-place, and foam’d at mouth, and was

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: speechless.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: ’Tis very like: he hath the falling-sickness.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: No, Caesar hath it not; but you, and I,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And honest Casca, we have the falling-sickness.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: I know not what you mean by that; but I am sure Caesar fell down. If

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: the tag-rag people did not clap him and hiss him, according as he

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: pleased and displeased them, as they use to do the players in the

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: theatre, I am no true man.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What said he when he came unto himself?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Marry, before he fell down, when he perceived the common herd was glad

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: he refused the crown, he pluck’d me ope his doublet, and offer’d them

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: his throat to cut. And I had been a man of any occupation, if I would

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: not have taken him at a word, I would I might go to hell among the

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: rogues. And so he fell. When he came to himself again, he said, if he

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: had done or said anything amiss, he desir’d their worships to think it

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: was his infirmity. Three or four wenches where I stood cried, “Alas,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: good soul!” and forgave him with all their hearts. But there’s no heed

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: to be taken of them: if Caesar had stabb’d their mothers, they would

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: have done no less.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And, after that, he came thus sad away?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Did Cicero say anything?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Ay, he spoke Greek.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To what effect?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Nay, and I tell you that, I’ll ne’er look you i’ the face again. But

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: those that understood him smil’d at one another and shook their heads;

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: but for mine own part, it was Greek to me. I could tell you more news

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: too: Marullus and Flavius, for pulling scarfs off Caesar’s images, are

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: put to silence. Fare you well. There was more foolery yet, if I could

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: remember it.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Will you sup with me tonight, Casca?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: No, I am promis’d forth.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Will you dine with me tomorrow?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Ay, if I be alive, and your mind hold, and your dinner worth the

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: eating.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Good. I will expect you.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Do so; farewell both.
[_Exit Casca._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What a blunt fellow is this grown to be!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He was quick mettle when he went to school.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: So is he now in execution

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Of any bold or noble enterprise,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: However he puts on this tardy form.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This rudeness is a sauce to his good wit,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Which gives men stomach to digest his words

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: With better appetite.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And so it is. For this time I will leave you:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Tomorrow, if you please to speak with me,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I will come home to you; or, if you will,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come home to me, and I will wait for you.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I will do so: till then, think of the world.
[_Exit Brutus._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Well, Brutus, thou art noble; yet I see,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Thy honourable metal may be wrought

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: From that it is dispos’d: therefore ’tis meet

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That noble minds keep ever with their likes;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For who so firm that cannot be seduc’d?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Caesar doth bear me hard, but he loves Brutus.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If I were Brutus now, and he were Cassius,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: He should not humour me. I will this night,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In several hands, in at his windows throw,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As if they came from several citizens,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Writings, all tending to the great opinion

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That Rome holds of his name; wherein obscurely

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Caesar’s ambition shall be glanced at.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And after this, let Caesar seat him sure,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For we will shake him, or worse days endure.
[_Exit._]
Thunder and lightning. Enter, from opposite sides, Casca with his sword drawn, and Cicero.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Good even, Casca: brought you Caesar home?

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Why are you breathless, and why stare you so?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Are not you moved, when all the sway of earth

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Shakes like a thing unfirm? O Cicero,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: I have seen tempests, when the scolding winds

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Have riv’d the knotty oaks; and I have seen

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Th’ ambitious ocean swell and rage and foam,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: To be exalted with the threatening clouds:

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: But never till tonight, never till now,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Did I go through a tempest dropping fire.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Either there is a civil strife in heaven,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Or else the world too saucy with the gods,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Incenses them to send destruction.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Why, saw you anything more wonderful?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: A common slave, you’d know him well by sight,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Held up his left hand, which did flame and burn

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Like twenty torches join’d, and yet his hand,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Not sensible of fire remain’d unscorch’d.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Besides, I ha’ not since put up my sword,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Against the Capitol I met a lion,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Who glared upon me, and went surly by,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Without annoying me. And there were drawn

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Upon a heap a hundred ghastly women,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Transformed with their fear; who swore they saw

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Men, all in fire, walk up and down the streets.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: And yesterday the bird of night did sit,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Even at noonday upon the marketplace,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Hooting and shrieking. When these prodigies

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Do so conjointly meet, let not men say,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: “These are their reasons; they are natural”;

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: For I believe, they are portentous things

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Unto the climate that they point upon.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Indeed, it is a strange-disposed time.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: But men may construe things after their fashion,

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Clean from the purpose of the things themselves.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Comes Caesar to the Capitol tomorrow?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: He doth, for he did bid Antonius

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Send word to you he would be there tomorrow.

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Goodnight then, Casca: this disturbed sky

lines.speaker: CICERO
lines.text: Is not to walk in.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Farewell, Cicero.
[_Exit Cicero._]
Enter Cassius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Who’s there?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: A Roman.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Casca, by your voice.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Your ear is good. Cassius, what night is this!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A very pleasing night to honest men.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Who ever knew the heavens menace so?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Those that have known the earth so full of faults.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For my part, I have walk’d about the streets,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Submitting me unto the perilous night;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And, thus unbraced, Casca, as you see,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Have bar’d my bosom to the thunder-stone;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And when the cross blue lightning seem’d to open

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The breast of heaven, I did present myself

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Even in the aim and very flash of it.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: But wherefore did you so much tempt the Heavens?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: It is the part of men to fear and tremble,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: When the most mighty gods by tokens send

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Such dreadful heralds to astonish us.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You are dull, Casca; and those sparks of life

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That should be in a Roman you do want,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Or else you use not. You look pale and gaze,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And put on fear and cast yourself in wonder,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To see the strange impatience of the Heavens:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But if you would consider the true cause

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Why all these fires, why all these gliding ghosts,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Why birds and beasts, from quality and kind;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Why old men, fools, and children calculate,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Why all these things change from their ordinance,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Their natures, and pre-formed faculties,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To monstrous quality; why, you shall find

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That Heaven hath infus’d them with these spirits,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To make them instruments of fear and warning

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Unto some monstrous state.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Now could I, Casca, name to thee a man

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Most like this dreadful night,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That thunders, lightens, opens graves, and roars,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As doth the lion in the Capitol;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A man no mightier than thyself, or me,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In personal action; yet prodigious grown,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And fearful, as these strange eruptions are.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: ’Tis Caesar that you mean; is it not, Cassius?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Let it be who it is: for Romans now

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Have thews and limbs like to their ancestors;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But, woe the while! our fathers’ minds are dead,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And we are govern’d with our mothers’ spirits;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Our yoke and sufferance show us womanish.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Indeed, they say the senators tomorrow

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Mean to establish Caesar as a king;

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: And he shall wear his crown by sea and land,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: In every place, save here in Italy.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I know where I will wear this dagger then;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Cassius from bondage will deliver Cassius:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Therein, ye gods, you make the weak most strong;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Therein, ye gods, you tyrants do defeat.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Nor stony tower, nor walls of beaten brass,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Nor airless dungeon, nor strong links of iron,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Can be retentive to the strength of spirit;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But life, being weary of these worldly bars,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Never lacks power to dismiss itself.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If I know this, know all the world besides,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That part of tyranny that I do bear

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I can shake off at pleasure.
[_Thunder still._]

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: So can I:

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: So every bondman in his own hand bears

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: The power to cancel his captivity.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And why should Caesar be a tyrant then?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Poor man! I know he would not be a wolf,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But that he sees the Romans are but sheep:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: He were no lion, were not Romans hinds.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Those that with haste will make a mighty fire

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Begin it with weak straws. What trash is Rome,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What rubbish, and what offal, when it serves

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For the base matter to illuminate

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: So vile a thing as Caesar! But, O grief,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Where hast thou led me? I, perhaps, speak this

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Before a willing bondman: then I know

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: My answer must be made; but I am arm’d,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And dangers are to me indifferent.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: You speak to Casca, and to such a man

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: That is no fleering tell-tale. Hold, my hand:

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Be factious for redress of all these griefs,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: And I will set this foot of mine as far

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: As who goes farthest.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: There’s a bargain made.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Now know you, Casca, I have mov’d already

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Some certain of the noblest-minded Romans

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To undergo with me an enterprise

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Of honourable-dangerous consequence;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And I do know by this, they stay for me

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In Pompey’s Porch: for now, this fearful night,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: There is no stir or walking in the streets;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And the complexion of the element

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In favour’s like the work we have in hand,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Most bloody, fiery, and most terrible.
Enter Cinna.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Stand close awhile, for here comes one in haste.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: ’Tis Cinna; I do know him by his gait;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: He is a friend. Cinna, where haste you so?

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: To find out you. Who’s that? Metellus Cimber?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: No, it is Casca, one incorporate

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To our attempts. Am I not stay’d for, Cinna?

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: I am glad on’t. What a fearful night is this!

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: There’s two or three of us have seen strange sights.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Am I not stay’d for? tell me.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Yes, you are. O Cassius, if you could

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: But win the noble Brutus to our party—

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Be you content. Good Cinna, take this paper,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And look you lay it in the praetor’s chair,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Where Brutus may but find it; and throw this

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In at his window; set this up with wax

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Upon old Brutus’ statue: all this done,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Repair to Pompey’s Porch, where you shall find us.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Is Decius Brutus and Trebonius there?

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: All but Metellus Cimber, and he’s gone

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: To seek you at your house. Well, I will hie,

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: And so bestow these papers as you bade me.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That done, repair to Pompey’s theatre.
[_Exit Cinna._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Come, Casca, you and I will yet, ere day,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: See Brutus at his house: three parts of him

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Is ours already, and the man entire

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Upon the next encounter, yields him ours.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: O, he sits high in all the people’s hearts!

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: And that which would appear offence in us,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: His countenance, like richest alchemy,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Will change to virtue and to worthiness.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Him, and his worth, and our great need of him,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You have right well conceited. Let us go,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For it is after midnight; and ere day,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: We will awake him, and be sure of him.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Brutus.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What, Lucius, ho!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I cannot, by the progress of the stars,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Give guess how near to day.—Lucius, I say!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I would it were my fault to sleep so soundly.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When, Lucius, when? Awake, I say! What, Lucius!
Enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Call’d you, my lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Get me a taper in my study, Lucius:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When it is lighted, come and call me here.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I will, my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It must be by his death: and for my part,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I know no personal cause to spurn at him,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But for the general. He would be crown’d:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: How that might change his nature, there’s the question.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It is the bright day that brings forth the adder,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And that craves wary walking. Crown him?—that;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And then, I grant, we put a sting in him,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That at his will he may do danger with.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Th’ abuse of greatness is, when it disjoins

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Remorse from power; and, to speak truth of Caesar,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I have not known when his affections sway’d

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: More than his reason. But ’tis a common proof,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That lowliness is young ambition’s ladder,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Whereto the climber-upward turns his face;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But when he once attains the upmost round,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He then unto the ladder turns his back,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Looks in the clouds, scorning the base degrees

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By which he did ascend. So Caesar may;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Then lest he may, prevent. And since the quarrel

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Will bear no colour for the thing he is,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Fashion it thus: that what he is, augmented,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Would run to these and these extremities:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And therefore think him as a serpent’s egg

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which hatch’d, would, as his kind grow mischievous;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And kill him in the shell.
Enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The taper burneth in your closet, sir.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Searching the window for a flint, I found

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: This paper, thus seal’d up, and I am sure

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: It did not lie there when I went to bed.
[_Gives him the letter._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Get you to bed again; it is not day.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is not tomorrow, boy, the Ides of March?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I know not, sir.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Look in the calendar, and bring me word.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I will, sir.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The exhalations, whizzing in the air

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Give so much light that I may read by them.
[_Opens the letter and reads._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: _Brutus, thou sleep’st: awake and see thyself.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Shall Rome, &c. Speak, strike, redress!_

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: “Brutus, thou sleep’st: awake!”

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Such instigations have been often dropp’d

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Where I have took them up.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: “Shall Rome, &c.” Thus must I piece it out:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Shall Rome stand under one man’s awe? What, Rome?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: My ancestors did from the streets of Rome

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The Tarquin drive, when he was call’d a king.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: “Speak, strike, redress!” Am I entreated

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To speak and strike? O Rome, I make thee promise,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If the redress will follow, thou receivest

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thy full petition at the hand of Brutus.
Enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sir, March is wasted fifteen days.
[_Knock within._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: ’Tis good. Go to the gate, somebody knocks.
[_Exit Lucius._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Since Cassius first did whet me against Caesar,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I have not slept.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Between the acting of a dreadful thing

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And the first motion, all the interim is

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Like a phantasma, or a hideous dream:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The genius and the mortal instruments

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Are then in council; and the state of man,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Like to a little kingdom, suffers then

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The nature of an insurrection.
Enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sir, ’tis your brother Cassius at the door,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Who doth desire to see you.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is he alone?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: No, sir, there are moe with him.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Do you know them?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: No, sir, their hats are pluck’d about their ears,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And half their faces buried in their cloaks,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That by no means I may discover them

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: By any mark of favour.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let ’em enter.
[_Exit Lucius._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: They are the faction. O conspiracy,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sham’st thou to show thy dangerous brow by night,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When evils are most free? O, then, by day

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Where wilt thou find a cavern dark enough

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To mask thy monstrous visage? Seek none, conspiracy;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hide it in smiles and affability:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For if thou path, thy native semblance on,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Not Erebus itself were dim enough

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To hide thee from prevention.
Enter Cassius, Casca, Decius, Cinna, Metellus Cimber and Trebonius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I think we are too bold upon your rest:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Good morrow, Brutus; do we trouble you?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I have been up this hour, awake all night.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Know I these men that come along with you?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Yes, every man of them; and no man here

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But honours you; and everyone doth wish

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You had but that opinion of yourself

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Which every noble Roman bears of you.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This is Trebonius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He is welcome hither.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This Decius Brutus.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He is welcome too.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This, Casca; this, Cinna; and this, Metellus Cimber.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: They are all welcome.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What watchful cares do interpose themselves

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Betwixt your eyes and night?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Shall I entreat a word?
[_They whisper._]

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Here lies the east: doth not the day break here?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: O, pardon, sir, it doth; and yon grey lines

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: That fret the clouds are messengers of day.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: You shall confess that you are both deceiv’d.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Here, as I point my sword, the Sun arises;

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Which is a great way growing on the South,

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Weighing the youthful season of the year.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Some two months hence, up higher toward the North

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: He first presents his fire; and the high East

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Stands, as the Capitol, directly here.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Give me your hands all over, one by one.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And let us swear our resolution.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No, not an oath. If not the face of men,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The sufferance of our souls, the time’s abuse—

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If these be motives weak, break off betimes,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And every man hence to his idle bed.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: So let high-sighted tyranny range on,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Till each man drop by lottery. But if these,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: As I am sure they do, bear fire enough

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To kindle cowards, and to steel with valour

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The melting spirits of women; then, countrymen,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What need we any spur but our own cause

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To prick us to redress? what other bond

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Than secret Romans, that have spoke the word,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And will not palter? and what other oath

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Than honesty to honesty engag’d,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That this shall be, or we will fall for it?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Swear priests and cowards, and men cautelous,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Old feeble carrions, and such suffering souls

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That welcome wrongs; unto bad causes swear

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Such creatures as men doubt; but do not stain

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The even virtue of our enterprise,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Nor th’ insuppressive mettle of our spirits,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To think that or our cause or our performance

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Did need an oath; when every drop of blood

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That every Roman bears, and nobly bears,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is guilty of a several bastardy,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If he do break the smallest particle

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Of any promise that hath pass’d from him.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But what of Cicero? Shall we sound him?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I think he will stand very strong with us.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Let us not leave him out.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: No, by no means.

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: O, let us have him, for his silver hairs

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Will purchase us a good opinion,

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: And buy men’s voices to commend our deeds.

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: It shall be said, his judgement rul’d our hands;

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Our youths and wildness shall no whit appear,

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: But all be buried in his gravity.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O, name him not; let us not break with him;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For he will never follow anything

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That other men begin.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Then leave him out.

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Indeed, he is not fit.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Shall no man else be touch’d but only Caesar?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Decius, well urg’d. I think it is not meet,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Mark Antony, so well belov’d of Caesar,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Should outlive Caesar: we shall find of him

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A shrewd contriver; and you know, his means,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If he improve them, may well stretch so far

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As to annoy us all; which to prevent,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Let Antony and Caesar fall together.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Our course will seem too bloody, Caius Cassius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To cut the head off, and then hack the limbs,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Like wrath in death, and envy afterwards;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For Antony is but a limb of Caesar.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let us be sacrificers, but not butchers, Caius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: We all stand up against the spirit of Caesar,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And in the spirit of men there is no blood.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O, that we then could come by Caesar’s spirit,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And not dismember Caesar! But, alas,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Caesar must bleed for it! And, gentle friends,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let’s kill him boldly, but not wrathfully;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let’s carve him as a dish fit for the gods,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Not hew him as a carcass fit for hounds.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And let our hearts, as subtle masters do,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Stir up their servants to an act of rage,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And after seem to chide ’em. This shall mark

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Our purpose necessary, and not envious;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which so appearing to the common eyes,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: We shall be call’d purgers, not murderers.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And for Mark Antony, think not of him;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For he can do no more than Caesar’s arm

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When Caesar’s head is off.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Yet I fear him;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For in the ingrafted love he bears to Caesar—

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Alas, good Cassius, do not think of him:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If he love Caesar, all that he can do

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is to himself; take thought and die for Caesar.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And that were much he should; for he is given

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To sports, to wildness, and much company.

lines.speaker: TREBONIUS
lines.text: There is no fear in him; let him not die;

lines.speaker: TREBONIUS
lines.text: For he will live, and laugh at this hereafter.
[_Clock strikes._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Peace! count the clock.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The clock hath stricken three.

lines.speaker: TREBONIUS
lines.text: ’Tis time to part.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But it is doubtful yet

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Whether Caesar will come forth today or no;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For he is superstitious grown of late,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Quite from the main opinion he held once

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Of fantasy, of dreams, and ceremonies.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: It may be these apparent prodigies,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The unaccustom’d terror of this night,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And the persuasion of his augurers,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: May hold him from the Capitol today.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Never fear that: if he be so resolved,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: I can o’ersway him, for he loves to hear

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: That unicorns may be betray’d with trees,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: And bears with glasses, elephants with holes,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Lions with toils, and men with flatterers.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: But when I tell him he hates flatterers,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: He says he does, being then most flattered.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Let me work;

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: For I can give his humour the true bent,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: And I will bring him to the Capitol.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Nay, we will all of us be there to fetch him.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By the eighth hour: is that the uttermost?

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Be that the uttermost; and fail not then.

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Caius Ligarius doth bear Caesar hard,

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Who rated him for speaking well of Pompey;

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: I wonder none of you have thought of him.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Now, good Metellus, go along by him:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He loves me well, and I have given him reason;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Send him but hither, and I’ll fashion him.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The morning comes upon’s. We’ll leave you, Brutus.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And, friends, disperse yourselves; but all remember

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What you have said, and show yourselves true Romans.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good gentlemen, look fresh and merrily;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let not our looks put on our purposes,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But bear it as our Roman actors do,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: With untired spirits and formal constancy.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And so, good morrow to you everyone.
[_Exeunt all but Brutus._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Boy! Lucius! Fast asleep? It is no matter;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Enjoy the honey-heavy dew of slumber:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thou hast no figures nor no fantasies,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which busy care draws in the brains of men;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Therefore thou sleep’st so sound.
Enter Portia.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Brutus, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Portia, what mean you? Wherefore rise you now?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It is not for your health thus to commit

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Your weak condition to the raw cold morning.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Nor for yours neither. Y’ have ungently, Brutus,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Stole from my bed; and yesternight at supper,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You suddenly arose, and walk’d about,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Musing and sighing, with your arms across;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And when I ask’d you what the matter was,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You star’d upon me with ungentle looks.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I urg’d you further; then you scratch’d your head,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And too impatiently stamp’d with your foot;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Yet I insisted, yet you answer’d not,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But with an angry wafture of your hand

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Gave sign for me to leave you. So I did,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Fearing to strengthen that impatience

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which seem’d too much enkindled; and withal

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Hoping it was but an effect of humour,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which sometime hath his hour with every man.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: It will not let you eat, nor talk, nor sleep;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And could it work so much upon your shape

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: As it hath much prevail’d on your condition,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I should not know you, Brutus. Dear my lord,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Make me acquainted with your cause of grief.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I am not well in health, and that is all.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Brutus is wise, and, were he not in health,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: He would embrace the means to come by it.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why, so I do. Good Portia, go to bed.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is Brutus sick, and is it physical

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To walk unbraced and suck up the humours

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of the dank morning? What, is Brutus sick,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And will he steal out of his wholesome bed

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To dare the vile contagion of the night,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And tempt the rheumy and unpurged air

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To add unto his sickness? No, my Brutus;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: You have some sick offence within your mind,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which, by the right and virtue of my place,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I ought to know of: and, upon my knees,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I charm you, by my once commended beauty,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: By all your vows of love, and that great vow

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which did incorporate and make us one,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That you unfold to me, your self, your half,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Why you are heavy, and what men tonight

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Have had resort to you; for here have been

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Some six or seven, who did hide their faces

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Even from darkness.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Kneel not, gentle Portia.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I should not need, if you were gentle Brutus.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Within the bond of marriage, tell me, Brutus,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is it excepted I should know no secrets

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That appertain to you? Am I your self

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: But, as it were, in sort or limitation,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: To keep with you at meals, comfort your bed,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And talk to you sometimes? Dwell I but in the suburbs

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Of your good pleasure? If it be no more,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Portia is Brutus’ harlot, not his wife.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You are my true and honourable wife,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: As dear to me as are the ruddy drops

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That visit my sad heart.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: If this were true, then should I know this secret.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I grant I am a woman; but withal

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A woman that Lord Brutus took to wife;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I grant I am a woman; but withal

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: A woman well reputed, Cato’s daughter.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Think you I am no stronger than my sex,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Being so father’d and so husbanded?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Tell me your counsels, I will not disclose ’em.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I have made strong proof of my constancy,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Giving myself a voluntary wound

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Here, in the thigh: can I bear that with patience

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And not my husband’s secrets?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O ye gods,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Render me worthy of this noble wife!
[_Knock._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hark, hark, one knocks. Portia, go in awhile;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And by and by thy bosom shall partake

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The secrets of my heart.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: All my engagements I will construe to thee,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: All the charactery of my sad brows.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Leave me with haste.
[_Exit Portia._]
Enter Lucius with Ligarius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucius, who’s that knocks?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Here is a sick man that would speak with you.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Caius Ligarius, that Metellus spake of.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Boy, stand aside. Caius Ligarius, how?

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Vouchsafe good-morrow from a feeble tongue.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O, what a time have you chose out, brave Caius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To wear a kerchief! Would you were not sick!

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: I am not sick, if Brutus have in hand

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Any exploit worthy the name of honour.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Such an exploit have I in hand, Ligarius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Had you a healthful ear to hear of it.

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: By all the gods that Romans bow before,

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: I here discard my sickness. Soul of Rome!

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Brave son, derived from honourable loins!

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Thou, like an exorcist, hast conjur’d up

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: My mortified spirit. Now bid me run,

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: And I will strive with things impossible,

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Yea, get the better of them. What’s to do?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: A piece of work that will make sick men whole.

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: But are not some whole that we must make sick?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That must we also. What it is, my Caius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I shall unfold to thee, as we are going,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To whom it must be done.

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: Set on your foot,

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: And with a heart new-fir’d I follow you,

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: To do I know not what; but it sufficeth

lines.speaker: LIGARIUS
lines.text: That Brutus leads me on.
[_Thunder._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Follow me then.
[_Exeunt._]
Thunder and lightning. Enter Caesar, in his nightgown.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Nor heaven nor earth have been at peace tonight:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Thrice hath Calphurnia in her sleep cried out,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: “Help, ho! They murder Caesar!” Who’s within?
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Go bid the priests do present sacrifice,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And bring me their opinions of success.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: I will, my lord.
[_Exit._]
Enter Calphurnia.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: What mean you, Caesar? Think you to walk forth?

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: You shall not stir out of your house today.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Caesar shall forth. The things that threaten’d me

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Ne’er look’d but on my back; when they shall see

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The face of Caesar, they are vanished.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Caesar, I never stood on ceremonies,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Yet now they fright me. There is one within,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Besides the things that we have heard and seen,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Recounts most horrid sights seen by the watch.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: A lioness hath whelped in the streets,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: And graves have yawn’d, and yielded up their dead;

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Fierce fiery warriors fight upon the clouds

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: In ranks and squadrons and right form of war,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Which drizzled blood upon the Capitol;

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: The noise of battle hurtled in the air,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Horses did neigh, and dying men did groan,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: And ghosts did shriek and squeal about the streets.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: O Caesar, these things are beyond all use,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: And I do fear them!

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What can be avoided

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Whose end is purpos’d by the mighty gods?

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Yet Caesar shall go forth; for these predictions

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Are to the world in general as to Caesar.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: When beggars die, there are no comets seen;

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: The heavens themselves blaze forth the death of princes.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Cowards die many times before their deaths;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The valiant never taste of death but once.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Of all the wonders that I yet have heard,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: It seems to me most strange that men should fear,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Seeing that death, a necessary end,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Will come when it will come.
Enter Servant.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What say the augurers?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: They would not have you to stir forth today.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Plucking the entrails of an offering forth,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: They could not find a heart within the beast.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The gods do this in shame of cowardice:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Caesar should be a beast without a heart

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: If he should stay at home today for fear.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: No, Caesar shall not. Danger knows full well

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That Caesar is more dangerous than he.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: We are two lions litter’d in one day,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And I the elder and more terrible,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And Caesar shall go forth.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Alas, my lord,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Your wisdom is consum’d in confidence.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Do not go forth today: call it my fear

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: That keeps you in the house, and not your own.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: We’ll send Mark Antony to the Senate-house,

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: And he shall say you are not well today.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Let me upon my knee prevail in this.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Mark Antony shall say I am not well,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And for thy humour, I will stay at home.
Enter Decius.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Here’s Decius Brutus, he shall tell them so.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Caesar, all hail! Good morrow, worthy Caesar.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: I come to fetch you to the Senate-house.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And you are come in very happy time

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: To bear my greeting to the Senators,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And tell them that I will not come today.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Cannot, is false; and that I dare not, falser:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I will not come today. Tell them so, Decius.

lines.speaker: CALPHURNIA
lines.text: Say he is sick.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Shall Caesar send a lie?

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Have I in conquest stretch’d mine arm so far,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: To be afeard to tell grey-beards the truth?

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Decius, go tell them Caesar will not come.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Most mighty Caesar, let me know some cause,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Lest I be laugh’d at when I tell them so.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The cause is in my will; I will not come.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That is enough to satisfy the Senate.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: But for your private satisfaction,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Because I love you, I will let you know:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Calphurnia here, my wife, stays me at home.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: She dreamt tonight she saw my statue,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Which like a fountain with an hundred spouts

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Did run pure blood; and many lusty Romans

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Came smiling, and did bathe their hands in it.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And these does she apply for warnings and portents

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And evils imminent; and on her knee

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Hath begg’d that I will stay at home today.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: This dream is all amiss interpreted:

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: It was a vision fair and fortunate.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Your statue spouting blood in many pipes,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: In which so many smiling Romans bath’d,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Signifies that from you great Rome shall suck

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Reviving blood, and that great men shall press

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: For tinctures, stains, relics, and cognizance.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: This by Calphurnia’s dream is signified.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And this way have you well expounded it.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: I have, when you have heard what I can say;

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: And know it now. The Senate have concluded

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: To give this day a crown to mighty Caesar.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: If you shall send them word you will not come,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Their minds may change. Besides, it were a mock

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Apt to be render’d, for someone to say,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: “Break up the Senate till another time,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: When Caesar’s wife shall meet with better dreams.”

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: If Caesar hide himself, shall they not whisper

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: “Lo, Caesar is afraid”?

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Pardon me, Caesar; for my dear dear love

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: To your proceeding bids me tell you this,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: And reason to my love is liable.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: How foolish do your fears seem now, Calphurnia!

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I am ashamed I did yield to them.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Give me my robe, for I will go.
Enter Brutus, Ligarius, Metellus, Casca, Trebonius, Cinna and Publius.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And look where Publius is come to fetch me.

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Good morrow, Caesar.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Welcome, Publius.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What, Brutus, are you stirr’d so early too?

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Good morrow, Casca. Caius Ligarius,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Caesar was ne’er so much your enemy

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: As that same ague which hath made you lean.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What is’t o’clock?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Caesar, ’tis strucken eight.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I thank you for your pains and courtesy.
Enter Antony.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: See! Antony, that revels long a-nights,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Is notwithstanding up. Good morrow, Antony.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: So to most noble Caesar.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Bid them prepare within.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I am to blame to be thus waited for.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Now, Cinna; now, Metellus; what, Trebonius!

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I have an hour’s talk in store for you:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Remember that you call on me today;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Be near me, that I may remember you.

lines.speaker: TREBONIUS
lines.text: Caesar, I will. [_Aside._] and so near will I be,

lines.speaker: TREBONIUS
lines.text: That your best friends shall wish I had been further.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Good friends, go in, and taste some wine with me;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And we, like friends, will straightway go together.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That every like is not the same, O Caesar,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The heart of Brutus yearns to think upon.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Artemidorus, reading a paper.

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: _“Caesar, beware of Brutus; take heed of Cassius; come not near Casca;

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: have an eye to Cinna; trust not Trebonius; mark well Metellus Cimber;

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: Decius Brutus loves thee not; thou hast wrong’d Caius Ligarius. There

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: is but one mind in all these men, and it is bent against Caesar. If

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: thou be’st not immortal, look about you: security gives way to

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: conspiracy. The mighty gods defend thee!

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: Thy lover, Artemidorus.”_ Here will I stand till Caesar pass along, And

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: as a suitor will I give him this. My heart laments that virtue cannot

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: live Out of the teeth of emulation. If thou read this, O Caesar, thou

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: mayest live; If not, the Fates with traitors do contrive.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Another part of the same street, before the house of Brutus.

lines.text: Enter Portia and Lucius.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I pr’ythee, boy, run to the Senate-house;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Stay not to answer me, but get thee gone.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Why dost thou stay?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: To know my errand, madam.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I would have had thee there and here again,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Ere I can tell thee what thou shouldst do there.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: O constancy, be strong upon my side,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Set a huge mountain ’tween my heart and tongue!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I have a man’s mind, but a woman’s might.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: How hard it is for women to keep counsel!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Art thou here yet?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Madam, what should I do?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Run to the Capitol, and nothing else?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And so return to you, and nothing else?

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Yes, bring me word, boy, if thy lord look well,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: For he went sickly forth: and take good note

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What Caesar doth, what suitors press to him.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Hark, boy, what noise is that?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I hear none, madam.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Pr’ythee, listen well.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I heard a bustling rumour, like a fray,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And the wind brings it from the Capitol.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sooth, madam, I hear nothing.
Enter the Soothsayer.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Come hither, fellow:

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Which way hast thou been?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: At mine own house, good lady.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: What is’t o’clock?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: About the ninth hour, lady.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Is Caesar yet gone to the Capitol?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Madam, not yet. I go to take my stand,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: To see him pass on to the Capitol.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Thou hast some suit to Caesar, hast thou not?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: That I have, lady, if it will please Caesar

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: To be so good to Caesar as to hear me,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: I shall beseech him to befriend himself.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Why, know’st thou any harm’s intended towards him?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: None that I know will be, much that I fear may chance.

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Good morrow to you. Here the street is narrow.

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The throng that follows Caesar at the heels,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Of Senators, of Praetors, common suitors,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Will crowd a feeble man almost to death:

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: I’ll get me to a place more void, and there

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Speak to great Caesar as he comes along.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: I must go in.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Ay me, how weak a thing

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The heart of woman is! O Brutus,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: The heavens speed thee in thine enterprise!

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Sure, the boy heard me. Brutus hath a suit

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: That Caesar will not grant. O, I grow faint.

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Run, Lucius, and commend me to my lord;

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: Say I am merry; come to me again,

lines.speaker: PORTIA
lines.text: And bring me word what he doth say to thee.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rome. Before the Capitol; the Senate sitting.

lines.text: A crowd of people in the street leading to the Capitol. Flourish. Enter Caesar, Brutus, Cassius, Casca, Decius, Metellus, Trebonius, Cinna, Antony, Lepidus, Artemidorus, Publius, Popilius and the Soothsayer.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The Ides of March are come.

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Ay, Caesar; but not gone.

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: Hail, Caesar! Read this schedule.

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Trebonius doth desire you to o’er-read,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: At your best leisure, this his humble suit.

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: O Caesar, read mine first; for mine’s a suit

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: That touches Caesar nearer. Read it, great Caesar.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What touches us ourself shall be last serv’d.

lines.speaker: ARTEMIDORUS
lines.text: Delay not, Caesar. Read it instantly.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What, is the fellow mad?

lines.speaker: PUBLIUS
lines.text: Sirrah, give place.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What, urge you your petitions in the street?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Come to the Capitol.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Caesar enters the Capitol, the rest following. All the Senators rise.

lines.speaker: POPILIUS
lines.text: I wish your enterprise today may thrive.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What enterprise, Popilius?

lines.speaker: POPILIUS
lines.text: Fare you well.
[_Advances to Caesar._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What said Popilius Lena?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: He wish’d today our enterprise might thrive.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I fear our purpose is discovered.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Look how he makes to Caesar: mark him.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Casca, be sudden, for we fear prevention.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Brutus, what shall be done? If this be known,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Cassius or Caesar never shall turn back,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For I will slay myself.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Cassius, be constant:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Popilius Lena speaks not of our purposes;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For look, he smiles, and Caesar doth not change.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Trebonius knows his time, for look you, Brutus,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: He draws Mark Antony out of the way.
[_Exeunt Antony and Trebonius. Caesar and the Senators take their seats._]

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Where is Metellus Cimber? Let him go,

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: And presently prefer his suit to Caesar.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He is address’d; press near and second him.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Casca, you are the first that rears your hand.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Are we all ready? What is now amiss

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That Caesar and his Senate must redress?

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Most high, most mighty, and most puissant Caesar,

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Metellus Cimber throws before thy seat

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: An humble heart.
[_Kneeling._]

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I must prevent thee, Cimber.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: These couchings and these lowly courtesies

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Might fire the blood of ordinary men,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And turn pre-ordinance and first decree

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Into the law of children. Be not fond,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: To think that Caesar bears such rebel blood

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That will be thaw’d from the true quality

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: With that which melteth fools; I mean sweet words,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Low-crooked curtsies, and base spaniel fawning.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Thy brother by decree is banished:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: If thou dost bend, and pray, and fawn for him,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I spurn thee like a cur out of my way.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Know, Caesar dost not wrong, nor without cause

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Will he be satisfied.

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: Is there no voice more worthy than my own,

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: To sound more sweetly in great Caesar’s ear

lines.speaker: METELLUS
lines.text: For the repealing of my banish’d brother?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I kiss thy hand, but not in flattery, Caesar;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Desiring thee that Publius Cimber may

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Have an immediate freedom of repeal.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: What, Brutus?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Pardon, Caesar; Caesar, pardon:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As low as to thy foot doth Cassius fall,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To beg enfranchisement for Publius Cimber.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: I could be well mov’d, if I were as you;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: If I could pray to move, prayers would move me:

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: But I am constant as the northern star,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Of whose true-fix’d and resting quality

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: There is no fellow in the firmament.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: The skies are painted with unnumber’d sparks,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: They are all fire, and every one doth shine;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: But there’s but one in all doth hold his place.

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: So in the world; ’tis furnish’d well with men,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And men are flesh and blood, and apprehensive;

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Yet in the number I do know but one

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That unassailable holds on his rank,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Unshak’d of motion: and that I am he,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Let me a little show it, even in this,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: That I was constant Cimber should be banish’d,

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: And constant do remain to keep him so.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: O Caesar,—

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Hence! wilt thou lift up Olympus?

lines.speaker: DECIUS
lines.text: Great Caesar,—

lines.speaker: CAESAR
lines.text: Doth not Brutus bootless kneel?

lines.speaker: CASCA
lines.text: Speak, hands, for me!

lines.text: Hath done this deed on Caesar. For your part,

lines.text: To you our swords have leaden points, Mark Antony;

lines.text: Our arms in strength of malice, and our hearts

lines.text: Of brothers’ temper, do receive you in

lines.text: Why I, that did love Caesar when I struck him,

lines.text: Let each man render me his bloody hand.

lines.text: First, Marcus Brutus, will I shake with you;

lines.text: Gentlemen all—alas, what shall I say?

lines.text: My credit now stands on such slippery ground,

lines.text: That one of two bad ways you must conceit me,

lines.text: Either a coward or a flatterer.

lines.text: That I did love thee, Caesar, O, ’tis true:

lines.text: If then thy spirit look upon us now,

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: He says, for Brutus’ sake

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: He finds himself beholding to us all.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: ’Twere best he speak no harm of Brutus here!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: This Caesar was a tyrant.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Nay, that’s certain.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: We are blest that Rome is rid of him.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Peace! let us hear what Antony can say.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You gentle Romans,—

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Peace, ho! let us hear him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I come to bury Caesar, not to praise him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The evil that men do lives after them,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The good is oft interred with their bones;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: So let it be with Caesar. The noble Brutus

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Hath told you Caesar was ambitious.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: If it were so, it was a grievous fault,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And grievously hath Caesar answer’d it.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Here, under leave of Brutus and the rest,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: For Brutus is an honourable man,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: So are they all, all honourable men,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Come I to speak in Caesar’s funeral.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He was my friend, faithful and just to me;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But Brutus says he was ambitious,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And Brutus is an honourable man.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He hath brought many captives home to Rome,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Whose ransoms did the general coffers fill:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Did this in Caesar seem ambitious?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: When that the poor have cried, Caesar hath wept;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Ambition should be made of sterner stuff:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Yet Brutus says he was ambitious;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And Brutus is an honourable man.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You all did see that on the Lupercal

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I thrice presented him a kingly crown,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Which he did thrice refuse. Was this ambition?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Yet Brutus says he was ambitious;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And sure he is an honourable man.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I speak not to disprove what Brutus spoke,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But here I am to speak what I do know.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You all did love him once, not without cause;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: What cause withholds you then to mourn for him?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: O judgement, thou art fled to brutish beasts,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And men have lost their reason. Bear with me.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: My heart is in the coffin there with Caesar,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And I must pause till it come back to me.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Methinks there is much reason in his sayings.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: If thou consider rightly of the matter,

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Caesar has had great wrong.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Has he, masters?

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: I fear there will a worse come in his place.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Mark’d ye his words? He would not take the crown;

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Therefore ’tis certain he was not ambitious.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: If it be found so, some will dear abide it.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Poor soul, his eyes are red as fire with weeping.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: There’s not a nobler man in Rome than Antony.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Now mark him; he begins again to speak.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But yesterday the word of Caesar might

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Have stood against the world; now lies he there,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And none so poor to do him reverence.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: O masters! If I were dispos’d to stir

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Your hearts and minds to mutiny and rage,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I should do Brutus wrong and Cassius wrong,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Who, you all know, are honourable men.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I will not do them wrong; I rather choose

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To wrong the dead, to wrong myself and you,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Than I will wrong such honourable men.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But here’s a parchment with the seal of Caesar,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I found it in his closet; ’tis his will:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Let but the commons hear this testament,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Which, pardon me, I do not mean to read,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And they would go and kiss dead Caesar’s wounds,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And dip their napkins in his sacred blood;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Yea, beg a hair of him for memory,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And, dying, mention it within their wills,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Bequeathing it as a rich legacy

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Unto their issue.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: We’ll hear the will. Read it, Mark Antony.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: The will, the will! We will hear Caesar’s will.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Have patience, gentle friends, I must not read it.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: It is not meet you know how Caesar loved you.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You are not wood, you are not stones, but men;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And being men, hearing the will of Caesar,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: It will inflame you, it will make you mad.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: ’Tis good you know not that you are his heirs;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: For if you should, O, what would come of it?

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Read the will! We’ll hear it, Antony;

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: You shall read us the will, Caesar’s will!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Will you be patient? Will you stay awhile?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I have o’ershot myself to tell you of it.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I fear I wrong the honourable men

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Whose daggers have stabb’d Caesar; I do fear it.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: They were traitors. Honourable men!

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: The will! The testament!

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: They were villains, murderers. The will! Read the will!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You will compel me then to read the will?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Then make a ring about the corpse of Caesar,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And let me show you him that made the will.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Shall I descend? and will you give me leave?

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Come down.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Descend.
[_He comes down._]

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: You shall have leave.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: A ring! Stand round.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Stand from the hearse, stand from the body.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Room for Antony, most noble Antony!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Nay, press not so upon me; stand far off.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Stand back; room! bear back.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: If you have tears, prepare to shed them now.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You all do know this mantle. I remember

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The first time ever Caesar put it on;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: ’Twas on a Summer’s evening, in his tent,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: That day he overcame the Nervii.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Look, in this place ran Cassius’ dagger through:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: See what a rent the envious Casca made:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Through this the well-beloved Brutus stabb’d;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And as he pluck’d his cursed steel away,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Mark how the blood of Caesar follow’d it,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: As rushing out of doors, to be resolv’d

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: If Brutus so unkindly knock’d, or no;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: For Brutus, as you know, was Caesar’s angel.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Judge, O you gods, how dearly Caesar lov’d him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: This was the most unkindest cut of all;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: For when the noble Caesar saw him stab,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Ingratitude, more strong than traitors’ arms,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Quite vanquish’d him: then burst his mighty heart;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And in his mantle muffling up his face,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
