lines.text: Even at the base of Pompey’s statue

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Which all the while ran blood, great Caesar fell.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: O, what a fall was there, my countrymen!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Then I, and you, and all of us fell down,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Whilst bloody treason flourish’d over us.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: O, now you weep; and I perceive you feel

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The dint of pity. These are gracious drops.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Kind souls, what weep you when you but behold

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Our Caesar’s vesture wounded? Look you here,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Here is himself, marr’d, as you see, with traitors.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: O piteous spectacle!

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: O noble Caesar!

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: O woeful day!

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: O traitors, villains!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: O most bloody sight!

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: We will be revenged.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Revenge,—about,—seek,—burn,—fire,—kill,—slay,—let not a traitor live!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Stay, countrymen.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Peace there! Hear the noble Antony.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: We’ll hear him, we’ll follow him, we’ll die with him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Good friends, sweet friends, let me not stir you up

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To such a sudden flood of mutiny.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: They that have done this deed are honourable.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: What private griefs they have, alas, I know not,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: That made them do it. They’re wise and honourable,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And will, no doubt, with reasons answer you.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I come not, friends, to steal away your hearts.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I am no orator, as Brutus is;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But, as you know me all, a plain blunt man,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: That love my friend; and that they know full well

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: That gave me public leave to speak of him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: For I have neither wit, nor words, nor worth,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Action, nor utterance, nor the power of speech,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To stir men’s blood. I only speak right on.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I tell you that which you yourselves do know,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Show you sweet Caesar’s wounds, poor poor dumb mouths,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And bid them speak for me. But were I Brutus,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And Brutus Antony, there were an Antony

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Would ruffle up your spirits, and put a tongue

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: In every wound of Caesar, that should move

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The stones of Rome to rise and mutiny.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: We’ll mutiny.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: We’ll burn the house of Brutus.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Away, then! come, seek the conspirators.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Yet hear me, countrymen; yet hear me speak.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Peace, ho! Hear Antony; most noble Antony.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Why, friends, you go to do you know not what.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Wherein hath Caesar thus deserved your loves?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Alas, you know not; I must tell you then.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You have forgot the will I told you of.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Most true; the will!—let’s stay, and hear the will.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Here is the will, and under Caesar’s seal.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To every Roman citizen he gives,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To every several man, seventy-five drachmas.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Most noble Caesar! We’ll revenge his death.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: O, royal Caesar!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Hear me with patience.

lines.speaker: CITIZENS
lines.text: Peace, ho!

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Moreover, he hath left you all his walks,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: His private arbors, and new-planted orchards,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: On this side Tiber; he hath left them you,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And to your heirs forever; common pleasures,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To walk abroad, and recreate yourselves.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Here was a Caesar! when comes such another?

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Never, never. Come, away, away!

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: We’ll burn his body in the holy place,

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: And with the brands fire the traitors’ houses.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Take up the body.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Go, fetch fire.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Pluck down benches.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Pluck down forms, windows, anything.
[_Exeunt Citizens, with the body._]

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Now let it work. Mischief, thou art afoot,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Take thou what course thou wilt!
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: How now, fellow?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Sir, Octavius is already come to Rome.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Where is he?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: He and Lepidus are at Caesar’s house.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And thither will I straight to visit him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He comes upon a wish. Fortune is merry,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And in this mood will give us anything.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: I heard him say Brutus and Cassius

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Are rid like madmen through the gates of Rome.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Belike they had some notice of the people,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: How I had moved them. Bring me to Octavius.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Cinna, the poet, and after him the citizens.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: I dreamt tonight that I did feast with Caesar,

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: And things unluckily charge my fantasy.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: I have no will to wander forth of doors,

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Yet something leads me forth.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: What is your name?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Whither are you going?

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Where do you dwell?

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Are you a married man or a bachelor?

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: Answer every man directly.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Ay, and briefly.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Ay, and wisely.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Ay, and truly, you were best.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: What is my name? Whither am I going? Where do I dwell? Am I a married

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: man or a bachelor? Then, to answer every man directly and briefly,

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: wisely and truly. Wisely I say I am a bachelor.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: That’s as much as to say they are fools that marry; you’ll bear me a

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: bang for that, I fear. Proceed, directly.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Directly, I am going to Caesar’s funeral.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: As a friend, or an enemy?

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: As a friend.

lines.speaker: SECOND CITIZEN
lines.text: That matter is answered directly.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: For your dwelling, briefly.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Briefly, I dwell by the Capitol.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Your name, sir, truly.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: Truly, my name is Cinna.

lines.speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
lines.text: Tear him to pieces! He’s a conspirator.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: I am Cinna the poet, I am Cinna the poet.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: Tear him for his bad verses, tear him for his bad verses.

lines.speaker: CINNA
lines.text: I am not Cinna the conspirator.

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: It is no matter, his name’s Cinna; pluck but his name out of his heart,

lines.speaker: FOURTH CITIZEN
lines.text: and turn him going.

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Tear him, tear him! Come; brands, ho! firebrands. To Brutus’, to

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Cassius’; burn all. Some to Decius’ house, and some to Casca’s, some to

lines.speaker: THIRD CITIZEN
lines.text: Ligarius’. Away, go!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rome. A room in Antony’s house.

lines.text: Enter Antony, Octavius and Lepidus, seated at a table.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: These many then shall die; their names are prick’d.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Your brother too must die; consent you, Lepidus?

lines.speaker: LEPIDUS
lines.text: I do consent,—

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Prick him down, Antony.

lines.speaker: LEPIDUS
lines.text: Upon condition Publius shall not live,

lines.speaker: LEPIDUS
lines.text: Who is your sister’s son, Mark Antony.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He shall not live; look, with a spot I damn him.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But, Lepidus, go you to Caesar’s house;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Fetch the will hither, and we shall determine

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: How to cut off some charge in legacies.

lines.speaker: LEPIDUS
lines.text: What, shall I find you here?

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Or here, or at the Capitol.
[_Exit Lepidus._]

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: This is a slight unmeritable man,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Meet to be sent on errands. Is it fit,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: The three-fold world divided, he should stand

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: One of the three to share it?

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: So you thought him,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: And took his voice who should be prick’d to die

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: In our black sentence and proscription.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Octavius, I have seen more days than you;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And though we lay these honours on this man,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To ease ourselves of divers sland’rous loads,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He shall but bear them as the ass bears gold,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To groan and sweat under the business,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Either led or driven, as we point the way;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And having brought our treasure where we will,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Then take we down his load, and turn him off,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Like to the empty ass, to shake his ears,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And graze in commons.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: You may do your will;

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: But he’s a tried and valiant soldier.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: So is my horse, Octavius; and for that

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: I do appoint him store of provender.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: It is a creature that I teach to fight,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To wind, to stop, to run directly on,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: His corporal motion govern’d by my spirit.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And, in some taste, is Lepidus but so:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He must be taught, and train’d, and bid go forth:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: A barren-spirited fellow; one that feeds

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: On objects, arts, and imitations,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Which, out of use and stal’d by other men,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Begin his fashion. Do not talk of him

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But as a property. And now, Octavius,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Listen great things. Brutus and Cassius

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Are levying powers; we must straight make head.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Therefore let our alliance be combin’d,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Our best friends made, our means stretch’d;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And let us presently go sit in council,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: How covert matters may be best disclos’d,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And open perils surest answered.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Let us do so: for we are at the stake,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: And bay’d about with many enemies;

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: And some that smile have in their hearts, I fear,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Millions of mischiefs.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Before Brutus’ tent, in the camp near Sardis.

lines.text: Drum. Enter Brutus, Lucilius, Titinius and Soldiers; Pindarus meeting them; Lucius at some distance.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Stand, ho!

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Give the word, ho! and stand.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What now, Lucilius! is Cassius near?

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: He is at hand, and Pindarus is come

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: To do you salutation from his master.
[_Pindarus gives a letter to Brutus._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He greets me well. Your master, Pindarus,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: In his own change, or by ill officers,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hath given me some worthy cause to wish

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Things done, undone: but, if he be at hand,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I shall be satisfied.

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: I do not doubt

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: But that my noble master will appear

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Such as he is, full of regard and honour.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He is not doubted. A word, Lucilius;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: How he received you, let me be resolv’d.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: With courtesy and with respect enough,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: But not with such familiar instances,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Nor with such free and friendly conference,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: As he hath us’d of old.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thou hast describ’d

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: A hot friend cooling. Ever note, Lucilius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When love begins to sicken and decay

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It useth an enforced ceremony.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: There are no tricks in plain and simple faith;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But hollow men, like horses hot at hand,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Make gallant show and promise of their mettle;
[_Low march within._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But when they should endure the bloody spur,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: They fall their crests, and like deceitful jades

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sink in the trial. Comes his army on?

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: They meant this night in Sardis to be quarter’d;

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: The greater part, the horse in general,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Are come with Cassius.
Enter Cassius and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hark! he is arriv’d.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: March gently on to meet him.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Stand, ho!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Stand, ho! Speak the word along.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Stand!

lines.speaker: SECOND SOLDIER
lines.text: Stand!

lines.speaker: THIRD SOLDIER
lines.text: Stand!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Most noble brother, you have done me wrong.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Judge me, you gods; wrong I mine enemies?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And if not so, how should I wrong a brother?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Brutus, this sober form of yours hides wrongs;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And when you do them—

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Cassius, be content.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Speak your griefs softly, I do know you well.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Before the eyes of both our armies here,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which should perceive nothing but love from us,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let us not wrangle. Bid them move away;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Then in my tent, Cassius, enlarge your griefs,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And I will give you audience.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Pindarus,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Bid our commanders lead their charges off

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A little from this ground.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucilius, do you the like; and let no man

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come to our tent till we have done our conference.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucius and Titinius, guard our door.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Brutus and Cassius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That you have wrong’d me doth appear in this:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You have condemn’d and noted Lucius Pella

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For taking bribes here of the Sardians;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Wherein my letters, praying on his side

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Because I knew the man, were slighted off.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You wrong’d yourself to write in such a case.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In such a time as this it is not meet

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That every nice offence should bear his comment.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let me tell you, Cassius, you yourself

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Are much condemn’d to have an itching palm,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To sell and mart your offices for gold

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To undeservers.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I an itching palm!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You know that you are Brutus that speak this,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Or, by the gods, this speech were else your last.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The name of Cassius honours this corruption,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And chastisement doth therefore hide his head.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Chastisement!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Remember March, the Ides of March remember:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Did not great Julius bleed for justice’ sake?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What villain touch’d his body, that did stab,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And not for justice? What! Shall one of us,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That struck the foremost man of all this world

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But for supporting robbers, shall we now

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Contaminate our fingers with base bribes,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And sell the mighty space of our large honours

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For so much trash as may be grasped thus?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I had rather be a dog, and bay the moon,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Than such a Roman.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Brutus, bait not me,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I’ll not endure it. You forget yourself,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To hedge me in. I am a soldier, I,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Older in practice, abler than yourself

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To make conditions.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Go to; you are not, Cassius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I am.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I say you are not.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Urge me no more, I shall forget myself;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Have mind upon your health, tempt me no farther.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Away, slight man!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hear me, for I will speak.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Must I give way and room to your rash choler?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Shall I be frighted when a madman stares?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O ye gods, ye gods! Must I endure all this?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: All this? ay, more: fret till your proud heart break;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Go show your slaves how choleric you are,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And make your bondmen tremble. Must I budge?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Must I observe you? Must I stand and crouch

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Under your testy humour? By the gods,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You shall digest the venom of your spleen,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Though it do split you; for, from this day forth,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I’ll use you for my mirth, yea, for my laughter,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When you are waspish.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Is it come to this?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You say you are a better soldier:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let it appear so; make your vaunting true,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And it shall please me well. For mine own part,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I shall be glad to learn of noble men.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You wrong me every way, you wrong me, Brutus.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I said, an elder soldier, not a better:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Did I say better?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If you did, I care not.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: When Caesar liv’d, he durst not thus have mov’d me.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Peace, peace! you durst not so have tempted him.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I durst not?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What? durst not tempt him?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For your life you durst not.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Do not presume too much upon my love.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I may do that I shall be sorry for.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You have done that you should be sorry for.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For I am arm’d so strong in honesty,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That they pass by me as the idle wind,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which I respect not. I did send to you

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For certain sums of gold, which you denied me;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For I can raise no money by vile means:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By Heaven, I had rather coin my heart,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And drop my blood for drachmas, than to wring

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: From the hard hands of peasants their vile trash

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By any indirection. I did send

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To you for gold to pay my legions,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which you denied me: was that done like Cassius?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Should I have answer’d Caius Cassius so?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When Marcus Brutus grows so covetous,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To lock such rascal counters from his friends,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Be ready, gods, with all your thunderbolts,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Dash him to pieces!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I denied you not.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: You did.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I did not. He was but a fool

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That brought my answer back. Brutus hath riv’d my heart.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A friend should bear his friend’s infirmities;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But Brutus makes mine greater than they are.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I do not, till you practise them on me.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You love me not.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I do not like your faults.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A friendly eye could never see such faults.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: A flatterer’s would not, though they do appear

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: As huge as high Olympus.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Come, Antony, and young Octavius, come,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Revenge yourselves alone on Cassius,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For Cassius is a-weary of the world:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Hated by one he loves; brav’d by his brother;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Check’d like a bondman; all his faults observ’d,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Set in a note-book, learn’d and conn’d by rote,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To cast into my teeth. O, I could weep

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: My spirit from mine eyes! There is my dagger,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And here my naked breast; within, a heart

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Dearer than Plutus’ mine, richer than gold:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If that thou be’st a Roman, take it forth.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I, that denied thee gold, will give my heart:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Strike as thou didst at Caesar; for I know,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: When thou didst hate him worst, thou lovedst him better

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Than ever thou lovedst Cassius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sheathe your dagger.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Be angry when you will, it shall have scope;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Do what you will, dishonour shall be humour.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O Cassius, you are yoked with a lamb

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That carries anger as the flint bears fire,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Who, much enforced, shows a hasty spark,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And straight is cold again.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Hath Cassius liv’d

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To be but mirth and laughter to his Brutus,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: When grief and blood ill-temper’d vexeth him?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When I spoke that, I was ill-temper’d too.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Do you confess so much? Give me your hand.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And my heart too.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O Brutus!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Have not you love enough to bear with me,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: When that rash humour which my mother gave me

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Makes me forgetful?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Yes, Cassius; and from henceforth,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: When you are over-earnest with your Brutus,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He’ll think your mother chides, and leave you so.
Enter Poet, followed by Lucilius, Titinius and Lucius.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Let me go in to see the generals,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: There is some grudge between ’em; ’tis not meet

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: They be alone.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: You shall not come to them.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Nothing but death shall stay me.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: How now! What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: For shame, you generals! What do you mean?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Love, and be friends, as two such men should be;

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: For I have seen more years, I’m sure, than ye.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Ha, ha! How vilely doth this cynic rhyme!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Get you hence, sirrah. Saucy fellow, hence!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Bear with him, Brutus; ’tis his fashion.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I’ll know his humour when he knows his time.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What should the wars do with these jigging fools?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Companion, hence!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Away, away, be gone!
[_Exit Poet._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucilius and Titinius, bid the commanders

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Prepare to lodge their companies tonight.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And come yourselves and bring Messala with you

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Immediately to us.
[_Exeunt Lucilius and Titinius._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucius, a bowl of wine.
[_Exit Lucius._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I did not think you could have been so angry.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O Cassius, I am sick of many griefs.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Of your philosophy you make no use,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If you give place to accidental evils.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No man bears sorrow better. Portia is dead.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Ha? Portia?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: She is dead.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: How ’scap’d I killing, when I cross’d you so?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O insupportable and touching loss!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Upon what sickness?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Impatient of my absence,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And grief that young Octavius with Mark Antony

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Have made themselves so strong; for with her death

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That tidings came. With this she fell distract,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And, her attendants absent, swallow’d fire.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And died so?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Even so.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O ye immortal gods!
Enter Lucius, with wine and a taper.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Speak no more of her. Give me a bowl of wine.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: In this I bury all unkindness, Cassius.
[_Drinks._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: My heart is thirsty for that noble pledge.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Fill, Lucius, till the wine o’erswell the cup.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I cannot drink too much of Brutus’ love.
[_Drinks._]
[_Exit Lucius._]
Enter Titinius and Messala.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come in, Titinius!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Welcome, good Messala.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Now sit we close about this taper here,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And call in question our necessities.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Portia, art thou gone?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No more, I pray you.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Messala, I have here received letters,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That young Octavius and Mark Antony

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come down upon us with a mighty power,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Bending their expedition toward Philippi.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Myself have letters of the selfsame tenor.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: With what addition?

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: That by proscription and bills of outlawry

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Octavius, Antony, and Lepidus

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Have put to death an hundred Senators.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Therein our letters do not well agree.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Mine speak of seventy Senators that died

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By their proscriptions, Cicero being one.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Cicero one!

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Cicero is dead,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: And by that order of proscription.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Had you your letters from your wife, my lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No, Messala.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Nor nothing in your letters writ of her?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Nothing, Messala.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: That, methinks, is strange.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why ask you? Hear you aught of her in yours?

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: No, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Now as you are a Roman, tell me true.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Then like a Roman bear the truth I tell,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: For certain she is dead, and by strange manner.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why, farewell, Portia. We must die, Messala.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: With meditating that she must die once,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I have the patience to endure it now.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Even so great men great losses should endure.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I have as much of this in art as you,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But yet my nature could not bear it so.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Well, to our work alive. What do you think

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Of marching to Philippi presently?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I do not think it good.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Your reason?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This it is:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: ’Tis better that the enemy seek us;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: So shall he waste his means, weary his soldiers,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Doing himself offence, whilst we, lying still,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Are full of rest, defence, and nimbleness.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good reasons must of force give place to better.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The people ’twixt Philippi and this ground

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Do stand but in a forced affection;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For they have grudg’d us contribution.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The enemy, marching along by them,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By them shall make a fuller number up,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come on refresh’d, new-added, and encourag’d;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: From which advantage shall we cut him off

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If at Philippi we do face him there,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: These people at our back.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Hear me, good brother.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Under your pardon. You must note besides,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That we have tried the utmost of our friends,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Our legions are brim-full, our cause is ripe.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The enemy increaseth every day;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: We, at the height, are ready to decline.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: There is a tide in the affairs of men,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Omitted, all the voyage of their life

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Is bound in shallows and in miseries.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: On such a full sea are we now afloat,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And we must take the current when it serves,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Or lose our ventures.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Then, with your will, go on:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: We’ll along ourselves, and meet them at Philippi.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The deep of night is crept upon our talk,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And nature must obey necessity,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which we will niggard with a little rest.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: There is no more to say?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: No more. Good night:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Early tomorrow will we rise, and hence.
Enter Lucius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucius! My gown.
[_Exit Lucius._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell now, good Messala.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good night, Titinius. Noble, noble Cassius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good night, and good repose.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O my dear brother!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This was an ill beginning of the night.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Never come such division ’tween our souls!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Let it not, Brutus.
Enter Lucius with the gown.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Everything is well.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Good night, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good night, good brother.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS and MESSALA
lines.text: Good night, Lord Brutus.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell, everyone.
[_Exeunt Cassius, Titinius and Messala._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Give me the gown. Where is thy instrument?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Here in the tent.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: What, thou speak’st drowsily?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Poor knave, I blame thee not, thou art o’er-watch’d.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Call Claudius and some other of my men;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I’ll have them sleep on cushions in my tent.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Varro and Claudius!
Enter Varro and Claudius.

lines.speaker: VARRO
lines.text: Calls my lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I pray you, sirs, lie in my tent and sleep;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It may be I shall raise you by-and-by

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: On business to my brother Cassius.

lines.speaker: VARRO
lines.text: So please you, we will stand and watch your pleasure.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I will not have it so; lie down, good sirs,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It may be I shall otherwise bethink me.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Look, Lucius, here’s the book I sought for so;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I put it in the pocket of my gown.
[_Servants lie down._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I was sure your lordship did not give it me.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Bear with me, good boy, I am much forgetful.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Canst thou hold up thy heavy eyes awhile,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And touch thy instrument a strain or two?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, my lord, an’t please you.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It does, my boy.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I trouble thee too much, but thou art willing.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: It is my duty, sir.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I should not urge thy duty past thy might;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I know young bloods look for a time of rest.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I have slept, my lord, already.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It was well done, and thou shalt sleep again;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I will not hold thee long. If I do live,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I will be good to thee.
[_Lucius plays and sings till he falls asleep._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: This is a sleepy tune. O murd’rous slumber,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Layest thou thy leaden mace upon my boy,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That plays thee music? Gentle knave, good night;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I will not do thee so much wrong to wake thee.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If thou dost nod, thou break’st thy instrument;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I’ll take it from thee; and, good boy, good night.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let me see, let me see; is not the leaf turn’d down

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Where I left reading? Here it is, I think.
Enter the Ghost of Caesar.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: How ill this taper burns! Ha! who comes here?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I think it is the weakness of mine eyes

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That shapes this monstrous apparition.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It comes upon me. Art thou anything?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Art thou some god, some angel, or some devil,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That mak’st my blood cold and my hair to stare?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Speak to me what thou art.

lines.speaker: GHOST
lines.text: Thy evil spirit, Brutus.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why com’st thou?

lines.speaker: GHOST
lines.text: To tell thee thou shalt see me at Philippi.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Well; then I shall see thee again?

lines.speaker: GHOST
lines.text: Ay, at Philippi.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why, I will see thee at Philippi then.
[_Ghost vanishes._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Now I have taken heart, thou vanishest.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ill spirit, I would hold more talk with thee.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Boy! Lucius! Varro! Claudius! Sirs, awake! Claudius!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The strings, my lord, are false.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He thinks he still is at his instrument.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lucius, awake!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Didst thou dream, Lucius, that thou so criedst out?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My lord, I do not know that I did cry.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Yes, that thou didst. Didst thou see anything?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Nothing, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sleep again, Lucius. Sirrah Claudius!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Fellow thou, awake!

lines.speaker: VARRO
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIUS
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why did you so cry out, sirs, in your sleep?

lines.speaker: VARRO. CLAUDIUS
lines.text: Did we, my lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ay. Saw you anything?

lines.speaker: VARRO
lines.text: No, my lord, I saw nothing.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIUS
lines.text: Nor I, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Go and commend me to my brother Cassius;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Bid him set on his powers betimes before,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And we will follow.

lines.speaker: VARRO. CLAUDIUS
lines.text: It shall be done, my lord.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Octavius, Antony and their Army.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Now, Antony, our hopes are answered.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: You said the enemy would not come down,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: But keep the hills and upper regions.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: It proves not so; their battles are at hand,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: They mean to warn us at Philippi here,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Answering before we do demand of them.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Tut, I am in their bosoms, and I know

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Wherefore they do it. They could be content

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To visit other places, and come down

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: With fearful bravery, thinking by this face

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: To fasten in our thoughts that they have courage;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: But ’tis not so.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Prepare you, generals.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The enemy comes on in gallant show;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Their bloody sign of battle is hung out,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And something to be done immediately.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Octavius, lead your battle softly on

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Upon the left hand of the even field.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Upon the right hand I. Keep thou the left.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Why do you cross me in this exigent?

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: I do not cross you; but I will do so.
[_March._]

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Drum. Enter Brutus, Cassius and their Army; Lucilius, Titinius, Messala

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: and others.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: They stand, and would have parley.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Stand fast, Titinius; we must out and talk.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Mark Antony, shall we give sign of battle?

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: No, Caesar, we will answer on their charge.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Make forth; the generals would have some words.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Stir not until the signal.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Words before blows: is it so, countrymen?

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Not that we love words better, as you do.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Good words are better than bad strokes, Octavius.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: In your bad strokes, Brutus, you give good words;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Witness the hole you made in Caesar’s heart,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Crying, “Long live! Hail, Caesar!”

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Antony,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The posture of your blows are yet unknown;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But for your words, they rob the Hybla bees,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And leave them honeyless.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Not stingless too.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O yes, and soundless too,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For you have stol’n their buzzing, Antony,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And very wisely threat before you sting.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Villains, you did not so when your vile daggers

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Hack’d one another in the sides of Caesar:

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: You show’d your teeth like apes, and fawn’d like hounds,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And bow’d like bondmen, kissing Caesar’s feet;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Whilst damned Casca, like a cur, behind

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Struck Caesar on the neck. O you flatterers!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Flatterers! Now, Brutus, thank yourself.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This tongue had not offended so today,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If Cassius might have rul’d.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Come, come, the cause. If arguing makes us sweat,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: The proof of it will turn to redder drops.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Look, I draw a sword against conspirators.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: When think you that the sword goes up again?

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Never, till Caesar’s three and thirty wounds

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Be well aveng’d; or till another Caesar

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Have added slaughter to the sword of traitors.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Caesar, thou canst not die by traitors’ hands,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Unless thou bring’st them with thee.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: So I hope.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: I was not born to die on Brutus’ sword.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O, if thou wert the noblest of thy strain,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Young man, thou couldst not die more honourable.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A peevish school-boy, worthless of such honour,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Join’d with a masker and a reveller.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Old Cassius still!

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Come, Antony; away!

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Defiance, traitors, hurl we in your teeth.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: If you dare fight today, come to the field;

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: If not, when you have stomachs.
[_Exeunt Octavius, Antony and their Army._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Why now, blow wind, swell billow, and swim bark!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The storm is up, and all is on the hazard.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ho, Lucilius! Hark, a word with you.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: My lord?
[_Brutus and Lucilius talk apart._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Messala.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: What says my General?

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Messala,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This is my birth-day; as this very day

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Was Cassius born. Give me thy hand, Messala:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Be thou my witness that against my will

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As Pompey was, am I compell’d to set

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Upon one battle all our liberties.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You know that I held Epicurus strong,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And his opinion. Now I change my mind,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And partly credit things that do presage.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Coming from Sardis, on our former ensign

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Two mighty eagles fell, and there they perch’d,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Gorging and feeding from our soldiers’ hands,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Who to Philippi here consorted us.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This morning are they fled away and gone,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And in their steads do ravens, crows, and kites

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Fly o’er our heads, and downward look on us,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: As we were sickly prey: their shadows seem

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: A canopy most fatal, under which

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Our army lies, ready to give up the ghost.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Believe not so.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I but believe it partly,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For I am fresh of spirit, and resolv’d

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To meet all perils very constantly.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Even so, Lucilius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Now, most noble Brutus,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The gods today stand friendly, that we may,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Lovers in peace, lead on our days to age!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: But, since the affairs of men rest still incertain,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Let’s reason with the worst that may befall.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If we do lose this battle, then is this

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: The very last time we shall speak together:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What are you then determined to do?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Even by the rule of that philosophy

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By which I did blame Cato for the death

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Which he did give himself, I know not how,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But I do find it cowardly and vile,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For fear of what might fall, so to prevent

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The time of life, arming myself with patience

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To stay the providence of some high powers

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That govern us below.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Then, if we lose this battle,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: You are contented to be led in triumph

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Thorough the streets of Rome?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: No, Cassius, no: think not, thou noble Roman,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That ever Brutus will go bound to Rome;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: He bears too great a mind. But this same day

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Must end that work the Ides of March begun;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And whether we shall meet again I know not.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Therefore our everlasting farewell take.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: For ever, and for ever, farewell, Cassius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If we do meet again, why, we shall smile;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: If not, why then this parting was well made.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: For ever and for ever farewell, Brutus.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If we do meet again, we’ll smile indeed;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: If not, ’tis true this parting was well made.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why then, lead on. O, that a man might know

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The end of this day’s business ere it come!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But it sufficeth that the day will end,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And then the end is known. Come, ho! away!
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. The field of battle.

lines.text: Alarum. Enter Brutus and Messala.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ride, ride, Messala, ride, and give these bills

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Unto the legions on the other side.
[_Loud alarum._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Let them set on at once; for I perceive

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: But cold demeanor in Octavius’ wing,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And sudden push gives them the overthrow.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Ride, ride, Messala; let them all come down.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Enter Cassius and Titinius.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O, look, Titinius, look, the villains fly!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Myself have to mine own turn’d enemy:

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This ensign here of mine was turning back;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: I slew the coward, and did take it from him.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: O Cassius, Brutus gave the word too early,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Who, having some advantage on Octavius,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Took it too eagerly: his soldiers fell to spoil,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Whilst we by Antony are all enclos’d.
Enter Pindarus.

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Fly further off, my lord, fly further off;

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Mark Antony is in your tents, my lord.

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Fly, therefore, noble Cassius, fly far off.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This hill is far enough. Look, look, Titinius;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Are those my tents where I perceive the fire?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: They are, my lord.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Titinius, if thou lovest me,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Mount thou my horse and hide thy spurs in him,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Till he have brought thee up to yonder troops

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And here again, that I may rest assur’d

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Whether yond troops are friend or enemy.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: I will be here again, even with a thought.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Go, Pindarus, get higher on that hill,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: My sight was ever thick. Regard Titinius,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And tell me what thou notest about the field.
[_Pindarus goes up._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: This day I breathed first. Time is come round,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And where I did begin, there shall I end.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: My life is run his compass. Sirrah, what news?
[_Above._]

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: O my lord!

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: What news?
[_Above._]

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Titinius is enclosed round about

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: With horsemen, that make to him on the spur,

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Yet he spurs on. Now they are almost on him.

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Now, Titinius! Now some light. O, he lights too.

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: He’s ta’en!
[_Shout._]

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: And, hark! they shout for joy.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Come down; behold no more.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: O, coward that I am, to live so long,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: To see my best friend ta’en before my face!
[_Pindarus descends._]

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Come hither, sirrah.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: In Parthia did I take thee prisoner;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And then I swore thee, saving of thy life,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That whatsoever I did bid thee do,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Thou shouldst attempt it. Come now, keep thine oath.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Now be a freeman; and with this good sword,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: That ran through Caesar’s bowels, search this bosom.

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Stand not to answer. Here, take thou the hilts;

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: And when my face is cover’d, as ’tis now,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Guide thou the sword.—Caesar, thou art reveng’d,

lines.speaker: CASSIUS
lines.text: Even with the sword that kill’d thee.
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: So, I am free, yet would not so have been,

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Durst I have done my will. O Cassius!

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Far from this country Pindarus shall run,

lines.speaker: PINDARUS
lines.text: Where never Roman shall take note of him.
[_Exit._]
Enter Titinius with Messala.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: It is but change, Titinius; for Octavius

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Is overthrown by noble Brutus’ power,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: As Cassius’ legions are by Antony.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: These tidings would well comfort Cassius.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Where did you leave him?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: All disconsolate,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: With Pindarus his bondman, on this hill.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Is not that he that lies upon the ground?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: He lies not like the living. O my heart!

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Is not that he?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: No, this was he, Messala,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: But Cassius is no more. O setting sun,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: As in thy red rays thou dost sink to night,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: So in his red blood Cassius’ day is set.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: The sun of Rome is set. Our day is gone;

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Clouds, dews, and dangers come; our deeds are done.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Mistrust of my success hath done this deed.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Mistrust of good success hath done this deed.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: O hateful Error, Melancholy’s child!

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Why dost thou show to the apt thoughts of men

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: The things that are not? O Error, soon conceiv’d,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Thou never com’st unto a happy birth,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: But kill’st the mother that engender’d thee!

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: What, Pindarus! where art thou, Pindarus?

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Seek him, Titinius, whilst I go to meet

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: The noble Brutus, thrusting this report

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Into his ears. I may say thrusting it;

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: For piercing steel and darts envenomed

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Shall be as welcome to the ears of Brutus

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: As tidings of this sight.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Hie you, Messala,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: And I will seek for Pindarus the while.
[_Exit Messala._]

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Why didst thou send me forth, brave Cassius?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Did I not meet thy friends? And did not they

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Put on my brows this wreath of victory,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: And bid me give it thee? Didst thou not hear their shouts?

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Alas, thou hast misconstrued everything!

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: But, hold thee, take this garland on thy brow;

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Thy Brutus bid me give it thee, and I

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Will do his bidding. Brutus, come apace,

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: And see how I regarded Caius Cassius.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: By your leave, gods. This is a Roman’s part.

lines.speaker: TITINIUS
lines.text: Come, Cassius’ sword, and find Titinius’ heart.
[_Dies._]
Alarum. Enter Brutus, Messala, young Cato, Strato, Volumnius and Lucilius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Where, where, Messala, doth his body lie?

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Lo, yonder, and Titinius mourning it.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Titinius’ face is upward.

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: He is slain.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: O Julius Caesar, thou art mighty yet!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thy spirit walks abroad, and turns our swords

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: In our own proper entrails.
[_Low alarums._]

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: Brave Titinius!

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: Look whether he have not crown’d dead Cassius!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Are yet two Romans living such as these?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The last of all the Romans, fare thee well!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It is impossible that ever Rome

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Should breed thy fellow. Friends, I owe more tears

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: To this dead man than you shall see me pay.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I shall find time, Cassius, I shall find time.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come therefore, and to Thassos send his body.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: His funerals shall not be in our camp,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Lest it discomfort us. Lucilius, come;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And come, young Cato; let us to the field.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Labeo and Flavius, set our battles on.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: ’Tis three o’clock; and Romans, yet ere night

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: We shall try fortune in a second fight.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Enter fighting soldiers of both armies; then Brutus, Messala, young Cato, Lucilius, Flavius and others.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Yet, countrymen, O, yet hold up your heads!

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: What bastard doth not? Who will go with me?

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: I will proclaim my name about the field.

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: A foe to tyrants, and my country’s friend.

lines.speaker: CATO
lines.text: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!
[_Charges the enemy._]

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: And I am Brutus, Marcus Brutus, I;

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Brutus, my country’s friend; know me for Brutus!
[_Exit, charging the enemy. Cato is overpowered, and falls._]

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: O young and noble Cato, art thou down?

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Why, now thou diest as bravely as Titinius,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: And mayst be honour’d, being Cato’s son.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Yield, or thou diest.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Only I yield to die:

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: There is so much that thou wilt kill me straight;
[_Offering money_]

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Kill Brutus, and be honour’d in his death.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: We must not. A noble prisoner!

lines.speaker: SECOND SOLDIER
lines.text: Room, ho! Tell Antony, Brutus is ta’en.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: I’ll tell the news. Here comes the General.
Enter Antony.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Brutus is ta’en, Brutus is ta’en, my lord.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Where is he?

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Safe, Antony; Brutus is safe enough.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: I dare assure thee that no enemy

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Shall ever take alive the noble Brutus.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: The gods defend him from so great a shame!

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: When you do find him, or alive or dead,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: He will be found like Brutus, like himself.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: This is not Brutus, friend; but, I assure you,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: A prize no less in worth. Keep this man safe,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Give him all kindness. I had rather have

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Such men my friends than enemies. Go on,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And see whether Brutus be alive or dead;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And bring us word unto Octavius’ tent

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: How everything is chanc’d.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Brutus, Dardanius, Clitus, Strato and Volumnius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come, poor remains of friends, rest on this rock.

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: Statilius show’d the torch-light; but, my lord,

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: He came not back: he is or ta’en or slain.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Sit thee down, Clitus. Slaying is the word;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It is a deed in fashion. Hark thee, Clitus.
[_Whispering._]

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: What, I, my lord? No, not for all the world.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Peace then, no words.

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: I’ll rather kill myself.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hark thee, Dardanius.
[_Whispers him._]

lines.speaker: DARDANIUS
lines.text: Shall I do such a deed?

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: O Dardanius!

lines.speaker: DARDANIUS
lines.text: O Clitus!

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: What ill request did Brutus make to thee?

lines.speaker: DARDANIUS
lines.text: To kill him, Clitus. Look, he meditates.

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: Now is that noble vessel full of grief,

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: That it runs over even at his eyes.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Come hither, good Volumnius; list a word.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIUS
lines.text: What says my lord?

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Why, this, Volumnius:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: The ghost of Caesar hath appear’d to me

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Two several times by night; at Sardis once,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: And this last night here in Philippi fields.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I know my hour is come.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIUS
lines.text: Not so, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Nay I am sure it is, Volumnius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thou seest the world, Volumnius, how it goes;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Our enemies have beat us to the pit.
[_Low alarums._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: It is more worthy to leap in ourselves

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Than tarry till they push us. Good Volumnius,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thou know’st that we two went to school together;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Even for that our love of old, I pr’ythee

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hold thou my sword-hilts, whilst I run on it.

lines.speaker: VOLUMNIUS
lines.text: That’s not an office for a friend, my lord.
[_Alarums still._]

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: Fly, fly, my lord! there is no tarrying here.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell to you; and you; and you, Volumnius.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Strato, thou hast been all this while asleep;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell to thee too, Strato.—Countrymen,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: My heart doth joy, that yet in all my life

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I found no man but he was true to me.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I shall have glory by this losing day

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: More than Octavius and Mark Antony

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: By this vile conquest shall attain unto.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: So fare you well at once; for Brutus’ tongue

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hath almost ended his life’s history.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Night hangs upon mine eyes; my bones would rest,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: That have but labour’d to attain this hour.
[_Alarums. Cry within, “Fly, fly, fly!”._]

lines.speaker: CLITUS
lines.text: Fly, my lord, fly!

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hence! I will follow.
[_Exeunt Clitus, Dardanius and Volumnius._]

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I pr’ythee, Strato, stay thou by thy lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thou art a fellow of a good respect;

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Thy life hath had some smatch of honour in it.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Hold then my sword, and turn away thy face,

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: While I do run upon it. Wilt thou, Strato?

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: Give me your hand first. Fare you well, my lord.

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: Farewell, good Strato.—Caesar, now be still:

lines.speaker: BRUTUS
lines.text: I kill’d not thee with half so good a will.
[_He runs on his sword, and dies._]
Alarum. Retreat. Enter Antony, Octavius, Messala, Lucilius and the Army.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: What man is that?

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: My master’s man. Strato, where is thy master?

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: Free from the bondage you are in, Messala.

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: The conquerors can but make a fire of him;

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: For Brutus only overcame himself,

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: And no man else hath honour by his death.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: So Brutus should be found. I thank thee, Brutus,

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: That thou hast prov’d Lucilius’ saying true.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: All that serv’d Brutus, I will entertain them.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Fellow, wilt thou bestow thy time with me?

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: Ay, if Messala will prefer me to you.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Do so, good Messala.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: How died my master, Strato?

lines.speaker: STRATO
lines.text: I held the sword, and he did run on it.

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: Octavius, then take him to follow thee,

lines.speaker: MESSALA
lines.text: That did the latest service to my master.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: This was the noblest Roman of them all.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: All the conspirators save only he,

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: Did that they did in envy of great Caesar;

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: He only, in a general honest thought

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And common good to all, made one of them.

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: His life was gentle, and the elements

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: So mix’d in him that Nature might stand up

lines.speaker: ANTONY
lines.text: And say to all the world, “This was a man!”

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: According to his virtue let us use him

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: With all respect and rites of burial.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Within my tent his bones tonight shall lie,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: Most like a soldier, order’d honourably.

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: So call the field to rest, and let’s away,

lines.speaker: OCTAVIUS
lines.text: To part the glories of this happy day.
[_Exeunt._]
